entries.title: Psalms 7:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Lest - Mine enemy. Tear - Out of my body.

entries.title: Psalms 7:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hands - Which Cush and others falsely lay to my charge. Iniquity - In my actions.

entries.title: Psalms 7:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Deliver - When it was in my power to destroy him, as 1Sam 24:2 - 6.

entries.title: Psalms 7:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Lift up - Glorify thyself, and shew thyself to be above them. Commanded - To execute that righteous sentence, which thou hast commanded, appointed, and declared by thy prophet Samuel.

entries.title: Psalms 7:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Compass - They will come from all parts to worship thee, and offer to thee praises and sacrifices. High - To thy tribunal, to sit there and judge my cause. An allusion to earthly tribunals, which generally are set up on high above the people.

entries.title: Psalms 7:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Every day - Even then, when his providence seems to favour them, and they are most secure and confident.

entries.title: Psalms 7:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: He will - God will hasten, and speedily execute his judgments upon him.

entries.title: Psalms 7:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Him - For the wicked. Ordaineth - Designs or fits for this very use. Of all sinners, persecutors are set up as the fairest marks of Divine wrath. They set God at defiance but cannot set themselves out of the reach of his judgments.

entries.title: Psalms 7:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Travelleth - This metaphor denotes his deep design, and vigorous endeavours for doing mischief, and his restlessness and pain 'till he have accomplished it.
